en.g: Decode headlines: why they drop little words and use short, punchy verbs.
p: Little words disappear: articles and be are dropped. CAT RESCUED FROM TREE = A cat was rescued from a tree.
Tense tricks: present simple = it just happened (TEAM WINS CUP), to + verb = future (QUEEN TO OPEN MUSEUM).
Short dramatic verbs: slash = cut, vow = promise, bid = attempt, clash = argue, quit = resign, boost = increase.
en.q: Have you ever seen an English headline that confused you? What do you think it really meant?
en.c: Rewrite three headlines as full sentences, e.g. FIRMS SLASH PRICES → Companies have cut their prices a lot.

de.g: Du entschlüsselst Schlagzeilen: Warum sie kleine Wörter weglassen und kurze, starke Verben nutzen.
p: Kleine Wörter fallen weg: Artikel und be. CAT RESCUED FROM TREE = A cat was rescued from a tree.
Zeit-Tricks: present simple = gerade passiert (TEAM WINS CUP), to + Verb = Zukunft (QUEEN TO OPEN MUSEUM).
Kurze, dramatische Verben: slash = cut, vow = promise, bid = attempt, clash = argue, quit = resign, boost = increase.
de.q: Hast du schon einmal eine englische Schlagzeile gesehen, die dich verwirrt hat? Was bedeutete sie wohl?
de.c: Schreib drei Schlagzeilen als ganze Sätze, z. B. FIRMS SLASH PRICES → Companies have cut their prices a lot.

es.g: Descifra titulares: por qué quitan palabras pequeñas y usan verbos cortos y directos.
p: Desaparecen palabras pequeñas: artículos y be. CAT RESCUED FROM TREE = A cat was rescued from a tree.
Trucos de tiempo: present simple = acaba de pasar (TEAM WINS CUP), to + verbo = futuro (QUEEN TO OPEN MUSEUM).
Verbos cortos y dramáticos: slash = cut, vow = promise, bid = attempt, clash = argue, quit = resign, boost = increase.
es.q: ¿Alguna vez te ha confundido un titular en inglés? ¿Qué crees que significaba de verdad?
es.c: Reescribe tres titulares como frases completas, p. ej. FIRMS SLASH PRICES → Companies have cut their prices a lot.

fr.g: Décode les gros titres : pourquoi ils suppriment les petits mots et utilisent des verbes courts.
p: Les petits mots disparaissent : articles et be. CAT RESCUED FROM TREE = A cat was rescued from a tree.
Astuces de temps : present simple = vient d'arriver (TEAM WINS CUP), to + verbe = futur (QUEEN TO OPEN MUSEUM).
Verbes courts et forts : slash = cut, vow = promise, bid = attempt, clash = argue, quit = resign, boost = increase.
fr.q: As-tu déjà vu un titre en anglais qui t'a dérouté ? Que voulait-il vraiment dire selon toi ?
fr.c: Réécris trois titres en phrases complètes, par ex. FIRMS SLASH PRICES → Companies have cut their prices a lot.

Trucchi dei tempi: present simple = appena successo (TEAM WINS CUP), to + verbo = futuro (QUEEN TO OPEN MUSEUM).
Verbi brevi e d'effetto: slash = cut, vow = promise, bid = attempt, clash = argue, quit = resign, boost = increase.
it.q: Ti è mai capitato un titolo in inglese che ti ha confuso? Cosa pensi che volesse dire?
it.c: Riscrivi tre titoli come frasi complete, ad es. FIRMS SLASH PRICES → Companies have cut their prices a lot.

pt.g: Descodifica manchetes: porque cortam as palavras pequenas e usam verbos curtos e fortes.
p: As palavras pequenas desaparecem: artigos e be. CAT RESCUED FROM TREE = A cat was rescued from a tree.
Truques de tempo: present simple = acabou de acontecer (TEAM WINS CUP), to + verbo = futuro (QUEEN TO OPEN MUSEUM).
Verbos curtos e dramáticos: slash = cut, vow = promise, bid = attempt, clash = argue, quit = resign, boost = increase.
pt.q: Já viste alguma manchete em inglês que te confundiu? O que achas que queria mesmo dizer?
pt.c: Reescreve três manchetes como frases completas, p. ex. FIRMS SLASH PRICES → Companies have cut their prices a lot.

en.g: Spot facts, opinions and exaggeration in what you read and hear.
p: A fact can be checked: Paris is the capital of France. An opinion is a belief: Paris is the most beautiful city.
Opinion signals: I think, I believe, the best, amazing, should. Exaggeration signals: always, never, everyone, the worst ever.
Challenge politely: Is that a fact or an opinion? What's the evidence? Where does that information come from?
en.q: Have you ever believed something online and later found out it wasn't true? What happened?
en.c: Write two facts and two opinions about your city, then add one exaggeration and mark which is which.

Meinungssignale: I think, I believe, the best, amazing, should. Übertreibung: always, never, everyone, the worst ever.
Höflich nachfragen: Is that a fact or an opinion? What's the evidence? Where does that information come from?
de.q: Hast du schon einmal online etwas geglaubt, das sich später als falsch herausstellte? Was war passiert?
de.c: Schreib zwei Fakten und zwei Meinungen über deine Stadt, dazu eine Übertreibung, und markiere, was was ist.

en.g: Learn how adverts speak: slogans, persuasive adjectives and urgency.
p: Imperatives talk to you directly: Try it today! Don't miss out! Treat yourself!
Persuasive adjectives: brand-new, long-lasting, natural, delicious, unbeatable, guaranteed, the best ever.
Urgency: limited offer, only three left, ends Sunday, while stocks last. Ask yourself: do I really need it?

en.g: Explain how you choose what to buy: brand, quality, value for money and reviews.

en.g: Use everyday money talk: saving, spending, budgets and what you can afford.
p: Verbs: save up for something, spend money on something, waste money, afford something, pay for something.
Lend vs borrow: you lend something to a friend, you borrow something from a friend. Can I borrow your charger?
Budget phrases: stick to a budget, cut down on, it's a bargain, it costs a fortune, I'm a bit short this month.

en.g: Suggest ideas to a group and react to other people's suggestions.
p: Base verb after Why don't we, Let's and We could: Why don't we go bowling? Let's meet at seven. We could cook together.
-ing or a noun after How about and What about: How about trying the new café? What about Saturday?
React: Sounds great! Good idea! I'm not so sure. Maybe another time. What if we... instead?
en.q: Your friends want to do something fun this weekend. What three suggestions would you make?
en.c: Plan a group outing in a short chat: write four suggestions, each with a different pattern, and two reactions.

-ing oder Nomen nach How about und What about: How about trying the new café? What about Saturday?
Reagieren: Sounds great! Good idea! I'm not so sure. Maybe another time. What if we... instead?

-ing o sustantivo tras How about y What about: How about trying the new café? What about Saturday?
Reacciona: Sounds great! Good idea! I'm not so sure. Maybe another time. What if we... instead?

en.g: Explain how something is made, using the passive and sequence words.
p: The passive focuses on the process: The cocoa beans are dried. Then they are roasted. Finally, the chocolate is shaped.
Made from (the material changes): Paper is made from wood. Made of (you can still see it): The table is made of oak.
Sequence words: first, then, next, after that, once, finally. Once the bread is baked, it is sliced and packed.
en.q: Do you know how your favourite food or drink is made? Can you explain one step of the process?
en.c: Explain how something is made, like bread or coffee, in five passive sentences with first, then, after that and finally.

Reihenfolge: first, then, next, after that, once, finally. Once the bread is baked, it is sliced and packed.

en.g: Solve problems together: define the problem, suggest options and agree on a solution.
p: Define it: What's the problem exactly? The main issue is that... We need to work out how to...
Test options with the first conditional: If we leave now, we'll miss the traffic. One option is to... Another is to...
Weigh it up and decide: The advantage is... The drawback is... On balance, let's go with option B.
